hints.title: Use the geometric sequence first
hints.body: Write its three terms in the stated order. Divide its second term by its first to find the common ratio, then write q in terms of p.
hints.recap: Consecutive geometric terms have the same ratio.
hints.pitfall: The two sequences put q in different positions.
hints.pause: Use your expression for q in the arithmetic sequence.

recall.reminder: Consecutive geometric terms have the same ratio.

hints.title: Use equal differences
hints.body: In the arithmetic sequence, subtract the first term from the second and the second from the third. Set these differences equal.
hints.recap: An arithmetic sequence has equal consecutive differences.
hints.pitfall: Keep only solutions that satisfy p<0.
hints.pause: Solve for p, then find q and the common difference.

recall.reminder: An arithmetic sequence has equal consecutive differences.

hints.title: Add the first ten terms
hints.body: Use Sn=n2[2a+(n−1)d] with the first term and common difference you found.
hints.recap: The sum formula uses the first term, not the second term.
hints.pitfall: Ten terms contain nine steps of the common difference.
hints.pause: Substitute and simplify the exact fraction.

recall.reminder: The sum formula uses the first term, not the second term.

solution:
In the GP, the ratio is p2p=p, because p<0 ensures p≠0. Hence its third term is q=p3. The AP condition gives 2q=p+p2, so 2p3−p2−p=p(2p+1)(p−1)=0.

The only negative root is p=−12. Then q=−18 and d=q−p=38. The requested AP sum is S10=5[2(−12)+9(38)]=5(198)=958, option B.

The GP ratio is used to determine the parameters; the final sum is of the AP, as requested.
knowledgePattern: Link reordered AP and GP terms to solve a cubic parameter constraint
